To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the RF control system is capable of providing a field stability that meets the specifications of the CEBAFs and TTFs RF systems, and the RF control system performance is limited by the cavity quality factor and the RF power source.

the performance of the RF feedback system can be predicted accurately using the tools described here, that a significant improvement in performance can be achieved by using digital feedback with feed forward, and that a digital system is more robust than analog systems against changes in the feedback loop parameters.
the TESLA linac RF system is very well suited to be operated with a feedback loop, and the performance of the CEBA F system can be improved by a factor of 2 to 3 with a feedback loop.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a feedback system for superconducting cavities.
the development of tools for performance analysis of superconducting RF linacs, in particular for systems with long RF pulse length.
a better understanding of the performance of RF systems with long RF pulses, which is essential to optimize the performance of the systems and to develop new concepts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RF system is well designed, and that the feedback system is capable of stabilizing the field to the required degree.
, in general, the performance of the RF control system is limited by the mechanical properties of the cavity and by the RF power source.
the RF system is stable and that the feedback is able to suppress the perturbations to an acceptable level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tools allow for a quick and reliable design and performance analysis for superconducting accelerator RF systems.
we are able to simulate the RF feedback system for a given design and obtain a quantitative measure for the quality of regulation.
the tools are a valuable design and performance analysis aid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of RF control systems is not only determined by the feedback controller, but also strongly influenced by the characteristics of the RF source, and the cavity.
the performance of the feedback system is limited by the noise in the power source and by the noise in cavity detuning, which is dominated by microphonics in the TESLA case.
the performance of a feedback system is strongly dependent on the frequency response of the controller.
